question: Pilot reports a strong fuel smell in the cockpit during ground run on a Robinson R44 Raven I. No visible fuel leak seen externally. Engine started and ran normally. What inspection should be performed?
expectedAnswer: 1. Shut down engine. Inspected carburetor (P/N 61C22451 MA-4-5) and all fuel connections for leaks. 2. Inspected carburetor float bowl drain screw - found loose (weeping fuel). Re-torqued drain screw to correct value. 3. Inspected carburetor gasket (P/N 66224) at mounting flange - no leak. 4. Inspected all fuel line connections from selector to carburetor for seeping fittings or cracked hoses. 5. Ground run post-repair - no fuel smell. Parts replaced: None (drain screw re-torqued).
notes: Imported from live DB. Key Points: Carburetor float bowl drain screw condition and torque; carburetor mounting gasket (P/N 66224) condition; fuel line connection integrity from fuel selector to carburetor; intake pipe hose clamp (P/N LW-15592-8-28) condition; presence of fuel residue at specific components to isolate source; post-repair ground run smell check.

question: Pilot reports OAT (outside air temperature) gauge pegged at full scale throughout the flight on a Robinson R44 Raven II. Carb air temperature gauge was normal. No other instrument anomalies. What troubleshooting and corrective action should be performed?
expectedAnswer: 1. Inspected B341 Outside Air Temp Gauge and O.A.T. Sender wiring (GREEN/BLACK/RED) at sender. 2. Measured sender resistance at ambient temperature - open circuit (sender failed). 3. Replaced O.A.T. sender (B341 OAT Sender). 4. Verified OAT gauge reads correct ambient temperature after replacement. 5. Inspected carb air temp sender (A058 Carb Air Temp Sender -17, wires 38/37/36) - serviceable and reading normally. Parts replaced: 1x OAT Sender (B341).
notes: Imported from live DB. Key Points: OAT sender resistance at known ambient temperature (open circuit = sender failed; note: pegged high usually indicates short to voltage or sender failure mode); wiring condition GREEN/BLACK/RED at sender connector; OAT gauge pointer behaviour (pegged high = short or specific failure mode); carb air temp sender (A058, wires 38/37/36) condition to confirm it is a separate independent circuit; post-replacement OAT gauge accuracy at ambient temperature.

question: Pilot reports collective push-to-start button inoperative on a Robinson R44 Raven I. Engine does not crank when collective start button is pressed. Engine starts normally using the ignition switch START position. What troubleshooting and corrective action should be performed?

notes: Imported from live DB. question: Pilot reports tail anti-collision strobe light inoperative on a Robinson R44 Raven I. Strobe LT switch confirmed ON. No circuit breaker tripped. Navigation and position lights are serviceable. CAR 605.16 compliance required. What troubleshooting and corrective action should be performed?

question: Pilot reports LOW OIL PRESSURE warning light ON in cruise at 2,500 ft ASL on a Robinson R44 Raven II with a Lycoming O-540-F1B5 engine. Verified oil pressure sender circuit continuity: wire #10 (P10 B), connector C2-6 - within spec. 5. Inspected all 6 rocker box cover gaskets (P/N 06B26669) - no seepage. 6. Engine ground run - oil pressure stabilised at 75 psi in green arc. Parts replaced: 1 qt Aeroshell W80+ consumed (no parts replaced).
notes: Imported from live DB. Key Points: Actual oil quantity vs. minimum limit; oil pressure relief valve spring free length vs. service limit; oil pressure sender circuit continuity at wire #10 (P10 B) connector C2-6; oil filler adapter and gasket condition for leaks; rocker box cover gasket condition; oil pressure reading at cruise power during ground run; OAT and power setting at time of event.

question: Pilot reports excessive left magneto RPM drop of 175 RPM (limit 125 RPM) on a Robinson R44 / Lycoming O-540-F1B5 during pre-flight run-up. Engine is rough on left magneto only. Right magneto drop is 50 RPM and within limits. What troubleshooting and corrective action should be performed?
expectedAnswer: 1. Removed top cowling. Inspected left magneto (P/N 66B21774, S6LSC-200), adapter (P/N LW-12707), and harness assembly LW-M-2463 for insulation damage and continuity. 2. Removed all 6 bottom spark plugs (Champion REM38E P/N 1182-E7) on left magneto circuit - cylinder #4 bottom plug found heavily fouled with lead deposits. 3. Cleaned all 6 plugs with plug cleaner/blaster; re-gapped all to Lycoming Maint. Manual limits. 4. Re-ran engine: left magneto drop 85 RPM - within limits. Right magneto unchanged. 5. Inspected magneto drive cushion (P/N 68H22624) and gaskets (P/N 62224) - serviceable. 6. Checked magneto timing - within limits per Lycoming Maint. Manual. Parts replaced: None (cyl #4 bottom plug cleaned and re-gapped).
notes: Imported from live DB. Key Points: Left vs. right magneto RPM drop comparison and maximum limit (125 RPM); which cylinder plugs are on the left magneto circuit; spark plug fouling type (lead, oil, carbon) and severity; spark plug gap measurement vs. Lycoming limits; harness LW-M-2463 continuity and insulation condition; magneto timing check; magneto drive cushion P/N 68H22624 condition; post-service magneto drop re-check.

question: Pilot reports oil sump gasket oil leak found dripping on the ground beneath the helicopter post-flight on a Robinson R44 Raven II with a Lycoming O-540-F1B5. Oil quantity is 1 quart low. What corrective action is required?

Re-installed oil sump with all studs and nuts to torque per Lycoming Maint. Manual. 7. Refilled engine with correct quantity and grade of oil. 8. Ground run - no oil leaks. Parts replaced: 1x Oil Sump Gasket P/N 06B21326; engine oil (consumable).

question: Pilot reports CLUTCH warning light ON during startup then again steadily during cruise on a Robinson R44 Raven I. Burning belt smell noted on shutdown. Belt tension actuator cycling noise heard during flight. What troubleshooting and corrective action should be performed?

question: Pilot reports oil residue on engine cowling after flight on a Robinson R44 Raven II with a Lycoming O-540-F1B5. AME post-flight inspection finds fresh oil seeping from a cylinder rocker box cover gasket. Oil quantity is normal. What corrective action is required?

Manual; condition of remaining 5 rocker box cover gaskets; post-repair ground run oil check.
